newsitem.title: UK: Intertanko sending envoy to secure tanker release.
newsitem.headline: Intertanko sending envoy to secure tanker release.

text.p: Intertanko is to send a special envoy to Venezuela in an attempt to help secure the release of the detained tanker Nissos Amorgos and its captain, the international association of independent tanker owners said Tuesday.

The Greek-owned 89,400dwt tanker Nissos Amorgos grounded in Venezuela's Maracaibo Channel on February 28 causing an oil spill. The vessel and its captain have been detained by the Venezuelan authorities since then.

Intertanko managing director Dagfinn Lunde said it was an unusual step to send a representative, but he hoped that Sybil Gosselin would be able to talk to everyone "and try to secure the release of the captain and enable the ship to proceed to a repair yard."
Gosselin, who speaks Spanish, heads Intertanko's Latin America sector.

The Nissos Amorgos was under the direction of a local pilot at the time of the accident, and Venezuela's Minister of Transport has said the ship probably struck the submerged wreck of a vessel, the Exportador, which sunk in 1988 and has yet to be cleared.
"No one in Venezuela seems to be suggesting that the captain or tanker were in any way at fault in this incident," Lunde said.
But local fishermen's unions have claimed pollution damages of $130 million which, according to Intertanko, have been more than doubled to $292.5 million to cover interest and legal fees.
Intertanko has argued from the outset that international pollution conventions signed by Venezuela should cover all compensation claims, and that there is no reason to detain the ship or its master.
Three tankers have grounded in the same section of the Maracaibo Channel this year. The Channel handles around 70 percent of Venezuela's oil exports,.
